INTRODUCTION OF SECRETARY-GENERAL, RAJYA SABHA 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I have great pleasure in 
introducing to the House the new Secretary-General, Dr. Yogendra

MEMBER SWORN 
Shri Ulit Suri (Uttar Pradesh) 
OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow 
to the passing away of Shri Rajendra Pratap Sinha alias Balajee, a 
former Member, Shri Narendra Mohan, a sitting Member, and Shri 
B. N. Banerjee, a former Member of this House. 
Shri Rajendra Pratap Sinha passed away on the 11* August, 
2002, at the age of 87. Bom at Arra h, Bihar, in August, 1915, Shri 
Sinha had his education at Surajpura, Hazaribagh and Allahabad. 
An agriculturist by vocation, Shri Sinha was actively 
associated with rural upliftment, village reconstruction and adult 
education. He was Secretary-General of the India-United Arab 
Friendship Association, In 1968. Shri Sinha also served as the 
Vice-chairman, Central Silk Board, in 1961. 
Shri Sinha represented the State of Bihar In this House for 
four consecutive terms from April, 1952 to April. 1954; April, 1964 
to April, 1980; April, 1960 to April, 1966, and again, from April, 1966 
to April, 1972. He was on the Panel of Vtce-Chairmen, Rajya 
Sabha from 1957 to 1958. 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [18 November, 2002] 
In the passing away of Shri Sinha, the country has lost an 
eminent parliamentarian and a noted social worker. 
Shri Narendra Mohan passed away on the 20* September, 
2002, at the age of 68, following multi-organ failure. Born at Kalpi. 
District Jalaun, Uttar Pradesh, in  October, 1934, Shri Narendra 
Mohan had his education at Kanpur. 
A journalist by profession, Shri Narendra Mohan was 
associated with various cultural, social, charitable organisations, 
and welfare institutions. He was the Chief-Editor of the Jagran 
group of newspapers. He also served as Chairman, Uttar Pradesh 
Sangeet Natak Academy, and Press Trust of India. Shri Narendra 
Mohan wrote a number of articles on different subjects and 
authored hundreds of poems and short stories in Hindi. He had 
several publications to his credit. For his outstanding contribution in 
the field of journalism, he was awarded the Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia 
Award in 1986. 
Shri Narendra Mohan represented the State of Uttar Pradesh 
in this House from November, 1996, till his death. A widely travelled 
person, Shri Narendra Mohan visited numerous countries for getting 
first-hand knowledge of the working and socio-economic conditions 
of newspapers and other industries. 
In the passing away of Shri Narendra Mohan, the country has 
lost a distinguished journalist and an active parliamentarian. 
Shri B.N. Banerjee passed away on the 4* October, 2002 at 
the age of 87. Bom at Berhampur, West Bengal, in January, 1916, 
and educated at Kolkata, London School of Economics and the 
Inner Temple, Shri Banerjee was a Member of the Bengal Judicial 
Service from 1942 to 1950. After a meritorious service there, Shri 
Banerjee joined the Ministry of Law,  Government of India, and also 
served as Legal Adviser to the High Commissioner of India in 
London. In 1956, he joined the Rajya Sabha Secretariat as Deputy 
Secretary, and was promoted to the post of Joint Secretary in 1980. 
In October, 1963, he was elevated to the post of Secretary, which 
was re-designated as Secretary-General, in 1973. He continued to 
hold this post up to March, 1976. 
Shri Banerjee had set a unique record of service to the House 
and helped in maintaining the highest traditions of Parliamentary 
System. As the 
2 

[18 November, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
Secretary-General, he helped in building up an impartial and 
efficient Secretariat to enable Members to fulfill their 
parliamentary role adequately. 
Shri Banerjee was nominated to this House in April, 1976, 
and remained a Member of this House till April, 1982. As a 
Member, he took keen interest in the proceedings of the House. 
In the passing away of Shri B.N. Banerjee, the country has 
lost an able administrator and a distinguished parliamentarian. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Rajendra 
Pratap Sinha, Shri Narendra Mohan  and Shri B. N. Banerjee. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe 
silence as a mark of respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute.) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the 
members of the bereaved familie s our sense of profound sorrow 
and deep sympathy. 
RE. DERAILMENT OF HOWRAH-NEW DELHI RAJDHANI 
EXPRESS 
MR. CHAIRMAN; Hon. Members, as you are aware, a 
tragedy took place on the 9* September, 2002, when the 
Howrah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express derailed near the approach 
of the Dhawa Bridge, between Rafiganj Station and Deo Road 
Block Hut Station, In Bihar. In this accident, the train locomotive 
and the first 16 coaches got derailed, and some of them got 
capsized also. In this unfortunate accident, 107 persons, 
including 22 railway staff, lost their lives, and 209 persons 
sustained injuries. The loss of so many precious lives had 
stunned the people of the country. The whole House extends its 
heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and also 
expresses sympathy and concern for those who had been 
injured. 
RE.TERRORIST ATTACK ON AKSHARDHAM TEMPLE, 
GANDHINAGAR 
MR. CHAIRMAN: I also refer with profound sorrow to the 
dastardly killing of 28 innocent pilgrims, including women and 
children, and causing injury to 84 others, by terrorists at 
Akshardham Temple Complex in Gandhi Nagar, Gujarat, on the 
24th September, 2002. In the operation to flush out the terrorists, 
one NSG commando and two Gujarat police personnel lost their 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [18 November, 2002] 
lives, setting an example of supreme sacrifice. The House 
condemns the cowardly attack on the innocent people within the 
temple premises. The House commends the exemplary courage 
with which the security personnel acted to gun down the terrorists 
and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. 
I would now request Members to rise in their places and 
observe silence as a mark of respect to the memory of those who 
lost their lives in these incidents. 
(Hon, Members then stood in silence for one minute.) 
RE. TAKING OF HOSTAGES BY TERRORISTS IN A THEATRE 
IN MOSCOW IN OCTOBER, 2002 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, last month, the world 
witnessed anothfiF cowardly and barbaric act ef terrorism when 
armed terrorists took several hundreds of innocent men, women 
and children as hostage in a theatre in-Moscow, on 23 rd October, 
2002. The Government of India had expressed its deep sympathy 
and solidarity with the Govern ment and the friendly people of 
Russia, with whom we share a close, warm and longstanding 
relationship. Our Government had also resolutory condemned this 
terrorist act. We are happy that hundreds of lives could be saved. 
On behalf of the people of India, whom this House represents, we 
convey our heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the families of 
the victims of the tragedy. We also wish to convey to our Russian 
brothers and sisters and to our fellow parliamentarians in the 
Russian Federation, that this House, which itself was the target of a 
terrorist attack last December, is one with them in their hour of grief 
and also in their resolution to fight the scourge of terrorism. 
India firmly condemns all acts of terrorism, wherever they may 
occur and whatever may be their motivation. Terrorism cannot be 
justified on any grounds and must be condemned unambiguously, 
wherever it exists. We also strongly condemn those who support 
terrorism or finance, train, harbour or support terrorists. India and 
Russia have both been victims of the global menace of terrorism. 
The Moscow Declaration on International Terrorism signed by the 
hon. Prime Minister and the President of the Russian Federation in 
Moscow last year reaffirmed our commitment to fight terrorism in all 
its forms.    The terrible terrorist act in Moscow is another 
4 

[18 November, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
reminder to the international community that the global phenomenon 
Of terrorism can be defeated only through global, combined, 
comprehensive, determined, sustained and long-term efforts.
